recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a dedicated study web-location element is desired again, handle it as a new work-group decision because the R5/R6 issue history intentionally superseded FHIR-31646.
issue_request: FHIR-31646 was a Published/Persuasive R5 BR&R change request to add ResearchStudy.webLocation 0..* with type CodeableConcept and url uri, using ResearchStudyUrlType example codes for registry, recruitment, and contact pages.
initial_application: The requested element was historically applied. Commit d7dbd7689b50ed517e3900c4512399c2cf62d466 added ResearchStudy.webLocation, ResearchStudy.webLocation.type, and ResearchStudy.webLocation.url to source/researchstudy/structuredefinition-ResearchStudy.xml. Nearby commit 9175459a6ea354d82e8b09ca90574344bbe333d6 mentioned #31646 but only adjusted other ResearchStudy reference targets, so the element addition appears to have been an implicit application rather than a cleanly Jira-tagged commit.
additional_context: FHIR-36023 later changed webLocation.type to webLocation.classifier. FHIR-39187 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and explicitly decided to remove ResearchStudy.webLocation because it substantially overlapped with relatedArtifact, with URL guidance moved to relatedArtifact. Commit 8bebe1521cc0a1da6a7bc48ff788297b3c554478 implemented that removal. FHIR-49760 then replaced ResearchStudy.relatedArtifact for R6 with citeAs and relatesTo, and current ResearchStudy.relatesTo.target[x] accepts uri, canonical, Reference, Attachment, and markdown targets.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Re-adding ResearchStudy.webLocation would reverse later Published/Applied BR&R decisions and duplicate the current ResearchStudy relationship model. The current build-scope ResearchStudy source has no webLocation element.
